claims.content: The System Operator initiates an emergency point report to communicate the existence of an emergency condition requiring search and rescue efforts.

goal.raw_text: The System Operator initiates an emergency point report to communicate the existence of an emergency condition requiring search and rescue efforts.

claims.content: System Operator
An emergency condition requiring search and rescue efforts must exist, as the J3.1 message is specifically used to report such conditions.
The System Operator must perform an explicit action to initiate the report, as reporting on emergency points is restricted to 'operator action only'.
If reporting on a previously reported point, the Joint Unit (JU) must have additional or more current information on that point.

If assuming reporting responsibility (R²) from another unit, the previous unit must be declared inactive (via J7.0 ACT=0) or no periodic update must have been received for three consecutive intervals.
The System Operator initiates an emergency point report (J3.1) when there is a need to report the existence of an emergency condition requiring search and rescue efforts.

trigger.raw_text: The System Operator initiates an emergency point report (J3.1) when there is a need to report the existence of an emergency condition requiring search and rescue efforts.

claims.content: The System Operator initiates the report through operator action only.
The System Operator transmits a J3.1 message to report the existence of an emergency condition that requires search and rescue efforts.
The System Operator assigns a Track Number (TN) to the point, line, or area reported on the interface.
The System Operator reports the position using geodetic latitude/longitude values.
If reporting on a previously reported track/point, the System Operator includes the TN, Previously Reported as amplifying information in the J3.1 message.
The System Operator ensures the emergency point has a TN, Reference different from the TN, Previously Reported.
If IFF/SIF data is available, the System Operator transmits it in the J3.1 message containing the IFF/SIF modes and codes of the previously reported track for which the emergency point was initiated.
If reporting on a previously reported emergency point, the Joint Unit (JU) may report through operator action only when it has additional or more current information on the point.

If a J7.0 (ACT = 0) message is received on an emergency point declaring the unit with R² inactive, or if no periodic update is received for three consecutive update intervals, another JU may assume R² for the point by operator action only.
A JU assuming R² for an emergency point shall use the same TN Reference and the same value of TN Previously Reported as those reported by the previous reporting unit.

It is illegal to change a reference or emergency point to any other type of surveillance entity; the Reference TN used for such points shall not be used for other entity types except in normal TN reuse.
The emergency condition requiring search and rescue efforts is formally reported via a J3.1 message.
The reported point (emergency point) is assigned a unique Track Number (TN) by the reporting Joint Unit.
The position of the emergency point is reported using geodetic latitude/longitude values.
If the emergency point relates to a previously reported track or point, the J3.1 message includes the TN, Previously Reported as amplifying information.
The TN, Reference assigned to the emergency point is different from the TN, Previously Reported.
If IFF/SIF data is available, it is included in the J3.1 message containing the modes and codes of the previously reported track associated with the emergency point.
The latest Joint Unit to report the emergency point holds reporting responsibility (R²) for that point.
Alert indicators are not applied to J3.1 Emergency Point messages because such points cannot be filtered.
